name: B.Com (Hons)
title: B.Com Honours
intro: The deeper commerce route: admission, honours coursework and options for research and professional courses.

phases.title: Class 12 prerequisites
phases.summary: Commerce with Maths is preferred by several top colleges.
points: Honours courses often prefer Commerce with Accountancy and Maths in Class 12.
Some colleges accept students from other streams with an additional subject requirement.
Check the college’s subject-combination rules in its admission bulletin.
Build your Class 12 marks, because honours seats at top colleges close at high cut-offs.

phases.title: Admission cycle
phases.summary: CUET-UG is the main route for central universities; private colleges set their own rules.
points: Register for CUET-UG and pick the right domain subjects for B.Com (Hons).
Fill in the university’s counselling form and rank your preferred colleges.
Take part in seat allocation rounds and accept a seat on time.
Keep backups, such as B.Com programme seats, in case you miss your honours cut-off.

phases.title: Honours coursework
phases.summary: Deeper papers in accounting, finance, taxation and business analytics.
points: You study core honours papers such as Financial Accounting, Corporate Accounting, Cost and Management Accounting, Income Tax and Auditing.
You also study statistics, economics, business law and financial management in more depth than the programme degree.
Electives allow specialisation in areas such as banking, taxation, or analytics.
In the optional fourth year you can complete a research project or dissertation.

phases.title: Internships and professional courses
phases.summary: Combine honours with a professional qualification or a skill certification.
points: Honours students often prepare for CA Foundation, CS or CMA while studying.
Complete at least one internship in accounting, audit or finance.
Learn Excel, Tally and data tools such as Power BI.
Join finance and commerce societies of your college.

phases.title: After B.Com Honours
points: Careers in accounting, auditing, banking, tax and finance.
Higher study: MBA, M.Com, MA Economics and finance master’s degrees.
Many students apply to government and bank exams.
Research routes: M.Com, then UGC NET for teaching and research.
